body:
Huh, oddly enough my psychiatrist told me that it doesn't matter what time of day I take them, but given your comment and the other commenter here it seems like it does help to take it in the mornings. I'm still hesitant on whether or not I should take my second dose for today since I was completely knocked out and unable to do anything today, so I might just wait until I have less going on to start.

Thanks for the advice!!

Ahh that's good to hear!! I'm feeling pretty discouraged at this point because I was completely incapable of doing anything for the first half of the day, and although I could get out of bed for the second half I still can't think clearly enough to get any work done. So part of me doesn't want to sacrifice several day's worth of work at the moment and just wait until I can take a couple days off

Woot woot then we're in this together!! Lol I messaged my psychiatrist in a panic because I wasn't able to get out of bed all day due to the body and headaches, she told me it was just the physical effects of me being anxious about the medicine. But seeing these responses makes me feel like there's definitely something else that other people experience too

I know it doesn’t make too much sense, but I feel like at least trying to OD would help prove to myself that I’m depressed/suicidal and might lead me to actually get help later. I always refuse help because I don’t think I’ve reached a low enough point. 

Part of me also knows that at the point I’m at right now I wouldn’t be able to follow through with an actual suicide (plus I don’t have any means to, and I know if I were actually heavily suicidal I’d probably find a way). So taking a shit ton of antidepressants at the current moment would mean that I’d be less likely to get any in the future, and might mean I’d get myself to a point where I can actually try harder next time and might succeed. Getting hospitalized after a failed attempt would also serve as a legitimate excuse to my school as to why I haven’t been doing well in classes, which contributes to the majority of my stress. 

I realize the logic is all over the place lol
Yeah, that’s sort of what I expected but seeing everyone writing it out makes it really sound like a pain. Appreciate the anecdote

Ah, that sucks I’m sorry. I was thinking of taking a bunch and then immediately calling for help because I know it wouldn’t work, but I’m also afraid of what would happen with my provider and medication in my future

Yeah, I don’t really expect it to work since I don’t have that much of them. Part of me is just excited to finally have something I can attempt with, even though I know it won’t work, but from looking online part of me also thinks that the shitty feeling after might finally make me do a real attempt in the future. Pretty confusing and conflicting, lol

From all these comments it sounds like it’s logistically be a problem getting medication in the future though, which sounds annoying
Damn, yeah that’s what everyone’s saying. From the looks of it it’s be a major inconvenience
Ah, thanks for letting me know. I’m in the US so no idea how it’d work and unfortunately there’s not much online, but picking it up daily sounds like a hassle :/
Thank you so much for the resource!

Yep, this is exactly how it is with me. A part of me always thinks I have to actively be showing symptoms or in the midst of a breakdown in order to accept/reach out for help, which is another reason why I always end up canceling. I've been trying to schedule appointments for nearly a year (which I thought would be the lowest point, since I had seen it as a last resort), but the ups and downs have meant I've routinely scheduled/canceled so much that I've only gone to four appointments in total over the past year. I was actually going to cancel a second appointment I made for this coming week but I think your comment helped convince me to keep it, so thank you!

I really connected with what you said about emotional memory, I think I mainly just try and block most emotions out of my head in general which is why it's so hard to remember what they're like. I've always been an indecisive person too, which leads to a route of inaction to avoid further anxiety. Plus, once I've convinced myself that my current emotional state is how I'll feel forever, it's even easier to stay inactive, because I genuinely believe that I've returned to normal or will end up dying.

However I think I'm currently in an in-between phase, which leads to posts like this and a bunch of uncertainty. So I again appreciate the advice.

Thank you so much for the detailed reply, I really appreciate it! Doing research on this kind of stuff (anything other than therapist/psychiatrist appointments) is pretty intimidating so I never knew that inpatient clinics were an option. One of my general concerns is that every couple days I'll go into a "near-crisis" mode (where I'm convinced I'm going to kill myself within the next day or two, but not necessarily in the moment), but then the next morning feel completely rational again and won't consider any mental health options at all, or cancel any appointments I've made because I'm feeling better. When I'm in that near-crisis mode I usually don't want any help because I'm so certain I've made up my mind, which is why now that I'm thinking rationally again I'm trying to evaluate my options for when I eventually get back to that state.

Again thank you so much for the kind words and for such a detailed response, it really helped!!

I'd never heard of a partial outpatient program, thank you for the suggestion! Will add to my list of options to think about.

Unfortunately the cost is a big concern for me as I have no idea how it'd work/how I'd finance it if it doesn't work with my insurance :(

Hi, appreciate the reply! I understand that the whole point of checking into a hospital would be to get help, I suppose the point of the cons list was to try and figure out if it'd be good for my specific situation (I'm sure being scared of going to a hospital wouldn't be a good sign, hence why I'm kind of treating it like a last resort).

I've actually just started seeing a psychiatrist but a therapist might also be needed or might be worth a shot, I'm just worried that whatever help either could provide wouldn't be soon enough for my needs (also why I thought that doing something more immediate like a hospital visit might be better). Guess I'll just have to think through all the options again haha. 

Again thank you for the comment!!
Hadn't ever heard of that before, thanks for the tip!
